clue.text: Will she wear only matching sets?

definitions.text: Will she wear only matching sets?

parts.words: Will she wear only matching sets?
parts.note: on a film set one crew member checks that costumes and props match from shot to shot, so the 'sets' are film sets, not outfits

explanation.surface: A fussy woman who will only put on coordinated outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' suggests clothing ensembles; it means film sets, where this crew member makes sure details stay consistent between takes.
explanation.definitionFit: This film-crew role keeps costume, props and staging consistent across scenes shot on different days.

clue.text: Company at Esher roundabout sticks together

indicators.note: a roundabout goes round, so the town's letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm drives round a traffic roundabout at Esher and stays in convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London; 'roundabout' signals the anagram, and the traffic roundabout of the surface is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold firmly together as one mass or whole.

clue.text: Lot, assuming Tom turns out a collector of bits and pieces

definitions.text: a collector of bits and pieces

indicators.note: turning out here means the words are shaken up and come out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the three words as printed give fourteen letters; the setter meant an extra I among them

explanation.surface: Lot takes on Tom, who proves to be a hoarder of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges LOT, ASSUMING and TOM, but those give only fourteen letters for fifteen: the second I is missing from the fodder as printed. 'Bits and pieces' are coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin collector or student of coinage, and 'bits' and 'pieces' are both old words for coins.

clue.text: Hard driver, of course

definitions.meaning: something hard and unyielding, like a metal, as in a will of this stuff
a golf club used to drive the ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: A tough motorist, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal is a byword for hardness, and on the golf course it is a club that hits the ball.

clue.text: Maintenance of raised part of castle

parts.note: raised means lifted up
the keep is the central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: The repair bill for a castle's elevated section.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair.

clue.text: Hilary, for example, breaks nail at the end

parts.note: Hilary is the name of a university and law term in Oxford and the English courts

indicators.note: breaks tells us the word nail is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A woman called Hilary snaps a fingernail at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a woman's name; it is the spring term at Oxford and the Inns of Court. 'breaks' signals that the nail's letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminal means final, coming at the close of something.

clue.text: Down-to earth matter included in this science?

definitions.text: Down-to earth matter included in this science?

parts.words: Down-to earth matter included in this science?
parts.note: read literally, a science dealing with the physical matter of the earth itself, not a sensible attitude

explanation.surface: Asking whether practical common sense is part of a scientific discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of science studies the physics of the planet: its gravity, magnetism and structure.

clue.text: Odd cruel finance, it turns out, for motorists to pay

indicators.note: what turns out is reshaped, so the three words are rearranged into a new phrase

explanation.surface: Drivers grumble about a strange and harsh charge they have to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: This was the British annual vehicle tax, once shown by a paper disc in the windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual British vehicle tax was paid by drivers before taking a car on public roads.

clue.text: Piece of lead shot — hide the French inside

indicators.note: inside places the French article within the animal skin

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's hide
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A hunter tells you to conceal the French in amongst the lead shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A single small ball of lead fired from a shotgun cartridge.

clue.text: Drake's place of retirement? Clumsy imitation

parts.note: ham means clumsy or inept, as in ham-fisted
a mock version is an imitation

explanation.surface: Ridiculing a clumsy copy of where Sir Francis Drake went to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Newbolt's poem 'Drake's Drum' has Drake asleep in his sailor's swinging bed, so 'retirement' means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor of Drake's era slept in a slung canvas bed, where Newbolt's poem places him at rest.

clue.text: Gear too outrageous for underground system

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of the two words are thrown about

explanation.surface: Outlandish kit fit for a subway network.
explanation.definitionFit: The network of roots a plant has below the soil.

clue.text: Reckless outbreak on the surface

definitions.meaning: a breaking out of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A careless eruption visible on top.
explanation.definitionFit: It means hasty and imprudent, and also a patch of spots breaking out on the skin.

clue.text: Gifted Hull, away, giving great pleasure

indicators.note: away suggests things going astray, so the letters of the two words are put in another order

explanation.surface: Talented Hull City playing away from home thrill their fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a city and football club in Yorkshire; 'away' rearranges GIFTED HULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Delightful describes what charms and pleases very much.

clue.text: Skilful treatment of board of directors?

definitions.meaning: the adroit handling of a person or situation
the people who run a company, collectively

explanation.surface: Asking whether the company board deals with things deftly.
explanation.definitionFit: It means deft handling of something, and also the body of people who run a business.

clue.text: Coal-layer has a name for tar

parts.note: a seam is a layer of coal underground

explanation.surface: A coal seam that includes a name for a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' is an old word for a sailor; the OCR text reads 'car', which the answer does not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, from the tarred clothing sailors wore.

clue.text: Fish I catch in old pram

parts.note: a bass is a fish
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: An angler hooks a fish in a baby carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded basket cradle, and also an old word for a baby carriage.

clue.text: Eastern dishes herein could not be taken out!

definitions.text: Eastern dishes herein could not be taken out!

parts.words: Eastern dishes herein could not be taken out!
parts.note: 'dishes' is slang for attractive women, kept secluded in an Eastern palace, not food from a takeaway

explanation.surface: Oriental food here was not available as a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishes' and 'taken out' suggest takeaway food; the dishes are beautiful women who could not be taken out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a Muslim household or palace, closed to outsiders.

clue.text: Deceitful pair confronted

parts.note: a pair is two
faced means confronted

explanation.surface: A couple are challenged with being dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocritical, showing one face to some people and another face to others.

clue.text: Indicator of lorry

definitions.meaning: one who tips, gives a hint or pointer
a truck whose body tilts to unload

explanation.surface: A truck's flashing direction light.
explanation.definitionFit: One who gives a tip points the way; and a dump truck is called by this name.

clue.text: Fashion-figure in Stone?

parts.note: read as a verb phrase, to fashion a figure in stone, not a fashion model in a magazine called Stone

explanation.surface: A celebrity model appearing in some publication called Stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve or model a shape out of stone or clay.

clue.text: Signs of DTs-endless regret after time

indicators.note: after puts the shortened regret behind the time letter
without its end, the regret loses its final letter

parts.note: remorse is regret

explanation.surface: A drinker's lingering regret over time spent.
explanation.walkthrough: DTs are delirium tremens, the shaking of alcohol withdrawal; 'endless' drops the last E of REMORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakings or shivers are a symptom of alcoholic withdrawal.

clue.text: Distort what was studied at Camptown?

parts.note: in Stephen Foster's song 'Camptown Races', 'the' is sung as 'de', so this is the article in that dialect
punters study the racing form before betting

explanation.surface: Twisting the facts about what people pored over at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camptown Races' (doo-dah) is a minstrel song about horse racing; racegoers study the form, which there becomes 'de form'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deform is to twist or warp something out of its proper shape.

clue.text: At a concert, is he at the front?

definitions.text: At a concert, is he at the front?

parts.words: At a concert, is he at the front?
parts.note: the standing audience at London's summer Proms gather right by the stage, and 'front' also suggests a seaside promenade

explanation.surface: Asking whether a concertgoer has got to the front row.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are London's summer classical concerts; standing ticket-holders fill the arena in front of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Proms concertgoer standing in the arena, or someone strolling along a seafront.

clue.text: Suffering this, good service round hospital is needed

indicators.note: round means the tennis serve encloses the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player in pain needs a hospital visit after a fine serve.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: A former line of relief for the poor

parts.note: the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a British line merged into British Rail in 1948

explanation.surface: An old railway once carried aid to the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS was one of Britain's big four railway companies before nationalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts of money or food given to those in need.

clue.text: Living close to ground, earth hog spills ale

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
a hog is a pig

indicators.note: spilled drink lands in a mess, so the word ale is jumbled

explanation.surface: A ground-dwelling pig knocks over some beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and zoology it describes growth or life on or just above the soil surface.

clue.text: He will open play dramatically (or achieve a duck)

parts.note: taken as written
to land a deal is to achieve it
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: An opening batsman will either play flamboyantly or be out for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The hero of Shakespeare's As You Like It speaks the play's first line; the cricket surface hides that 'open' is about drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of As You Like It delivers the opening speech of the comedy.

clue.text: Managers of Watford and Crewe, for instance, turning teams into stars

definitions.text: Managers of Watford and Crewe, for instance

indicators.note: turning here means the letters of the phrase are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Football bosses at Watford and Crewe Alexandra make their sides into stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Watford and Crewe are towns with football clubs and railway stations; Crewe is a famous junction, so the managers run stations, not teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway officials in charge of a stop, and both towns have well-known stations.
